name: CapCut Slide-On Photo Stack
use_when: A talking-head video needs supporting photos, real estate images, travel images, or proof visuals beside the speaker.
The footage was framed with negative space or rule-of-thirds placement to leave room for overlays.
A simple slide-in/out animation communicates more professionally than static images popping on.
avoid_when: The speaker was centered and photos would cover the face, hands, product, captions, or proof.
The images do not support the spoken point or make the screen feel cluttered.
The photo rights are unclear for the intended release.
A single full-screen image or B-roll clip would communicate more clearly.

timeline_pattern.pattern: speaker_framed_to_side -> photo_1_overlay -> resize_to_negative_space -> slide_in -> hold -> photo_2_offset_entry -> optional_slide_out -> clear_before_next_point
timeline_pattern.shooting_rule: Plan the speaker position while recording when photo overlays are expected later.
timeline_pattern.stagger_rule: Offset multiple photos so each entrance is readable instead of arriving in the same frame.
timeline_pattern.animation_rule: Use simple professional in/out animations, such as slide in from the side and slide back out.
timeline_pattern.hierarchy_rule: The speaker and first photo should not compete equally unless the segment intentionally becomes an image explanation.

motion.rule: Slide motion should be clean, consistent, and short enough that the photo is readable while the spoken point is active.

keyframe_values.slide_duration: Around 1.0-1.4 seconds can work for calm professional slide-ins; shorten for fast shorts after readability review.
keyframe_values.stagger_gap: Leave a visible gap between photo entrances so the viewer registers each image.
keyframe_values.size: Resize by composition, preserving face/caption space and avoiding tiny unreadable photos.
keyframe_values.exit: Use a matching slide-out or fade before the next visual stack competes.

sound.rule: Use no SFX or very light slide cues; photo stacks usually support speech rather than becoming impact transitions.

captions.rule: Photo overlays must be planned with caption placement; move or simplify captions if they collide with the photo stack.

color.rule: Photos should look consistent enough with the project palette; avoid clashing stock imagery that breaks the style lane.

implementation.ffmpeg: Overlay each image with timed x/y slide expressions, optional fade, and collision review contact sheets.
implementation.remotion: Model PhotoStack overlays with imageRefs, negativeSpaceRegion, inAnimation, startFrame, duration, outAnimation, and captionCollision metadata.
implementation.blender: Use image planes with 2D camera framing for branded photo boards or more dimensional slide-ins.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add each photo as an overlay, pinch-resize into planned negative space, add a simple Slide Right/Left in animation, offset later photos, and add matching out animations when the segment clears.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use image layers with Position keyframes or Essential Graphics animation presets; use guides/rulers to keep speaker and captions safe.

common_mistakes: Trying to add photos after filming without leaving screen space.
Covering the speaker's face, product, hands, or captions.
Making every photo enter at once so the viewer cannot parse them.
Using random stock photos that do not support the spoken point.
Leaving photos onscreen after the spoken reference has passed.
qc: Was the speaker framed with enough negative space for the photo stack?
Does each photo support the spoken point?
Do slide-ins and slide-outs finish before the viewer needs to inspect the image?
Do photos avoid faces, hands, captions, products, proof, and UI?
Are photo sources/license notes ready for publishable delivery?
